question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{{y}^{2}}(y-1)\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y-1)[{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{{y}^{2}}\,dx]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y-1)\,[x]_{{y}^{3}}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y-1)({y}^{2}-{y}^{3})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-{y}^{4}+2{y}^{3}-{y}^{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(-{y}^{4}+2{y}^{3}-{y}^{2})\,dy & ={[-\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}+\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{30}\end{aligned}
$$
